vignette: A 24-year-old woman with a two-week history of headache worse on lying down and transient visual obscurations has papilledema and a sixth nerve palsy. CT of the brain is normal. MR venography shows an absent flow signal in the right transverse sinus.
stem: What is the diagnosis and the mechanism of the sixth nerve palsy?

options.text: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension; the nerve is compressed in the cavernous sinus
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with raised pressure; the sixth nerve is stretched over the petrous ridge as a false localizing sign
Pontine glioma; the abducens nucleus is infiltrated
Migraine; the palsy is ophthalmoplegic migraine
Meningitis; the nerve is inflamed in the subarachnoid space

explanation: Headache, papilledema and a sixth nerve palsy with a normal CT mean raised intracranial pressure, and the absent transverse sinus flow makes the cause venous sinus thrombosis; the long intracranial course of the abducens nerve over the petrous apex makes it the nerve stretched by pressure, a false localizing sign that does not indicate a pontine lesion.
